units: feet, seconds; speeds in ft/s (1 mph = 1.4667 ft/s)

references.title: NHL EDGE Pro Reference Benchmarks

references.title: NHL EDGE Skating Stats Deep Dive 2025-26
references.usedFor: league-average top speed ~21.7 mph, distance per game

topSpeed.note: 27 to 33 ft/s = 18.4 to 22.5 mph; league-average top speed in simulated games is ~21.7 mph

effort.desc: share of top speed when not chasing, rushing or far from the spot

fatigue.desc: Shift fatigue. After startsAt seconds on the ice a skater loses top speed, acceleration and hands, reaching the full penalty at fullAt seconds. A unit stuck defending past 30-45 s is the case this models.

slap.usedWhen: defenseman or 45+ ft from the net

shot.note: wrist 58 to 85 mph, slap 80 to 100 mph

xg.desc: Context flags for the expected-goal model, matching MoneyPuck's definitions: a rebound is a shot within reboundWithinSec of the goalie's last save; a rush shot comes within rushWithinSec of the team's entry into the offensive zone.

puck.note: a 75 ft/s pass glides about 180 ft; a hard rim (70+ ft/s) keeps 88 percent of its speed off the boards so a dump wraps behind the net

freeze.desc: After a save the goalie covers the puck for a faceoff when an attacker is close enough to jam a rebound; otherwise he plays it or leaves a rebound.

goalie.tierGoalScaleNote: Multiplies the shot's expected goals (divided by the league on-net share) to get the goal probability against a league-average goalie; 0.72 lands goals per game at the league rate at the NHL-average settings, since the sim's shot mix still carries more medium-danger looks than the real game.

shotDecision.desc: When a carrier shoots. A clean look from the slot is a must-shoot (fires within a fraction of a second); everything else is a per-second probability scaled by shot quality, aggression and the shooter's rating. Shot quality is 0 to 1 from distance (75 ft horizon) and angle. Rates were retuned in 0.29 so that, at the NHL-average settings, unblocked attempts and the danger-tier mix match MoneyPuck's league rates with the expected-goal model scoring each shot.

perimeter.desc: A skater with a reasonable lane from the half wall, circles or point (28 to 55 ft) throws it at the net through traffic: that is where most NHL shots come from, and where most blocks happen.

inTight.desc: Puck on the stick in front of the goalie with no defender on him, within a second of getting it: shoot now. Only the goalie can stop this one, so no lane check.

breakaway.desc: An opponent counts as goal-side unless he is clearly behind the carrier (behindByFt); a wide opponent needs a bigger head start to be beaten.

dangerTiers.desc: Fallback only, used when the expected-goal model is not loaded. With the model, a shot's tier follows MoneyPuck's xG thresholds (low under 0.08, medium under 0.20, high 0.20 and up).

rulesBenchmarks.note: Approximate NHL per-team per-game rates. Icings: 10,264 icing events in the 2016-17 regular season (rjweise.github.io/Icing) over 1,230 games is about 8.3 per game, 4.2 per team. Offsides: roughly 6 per game league-wide from play-by-play stoppage counts, 3 per team.
